facts.label: cash from operations, Year to Jun 2026

what: It makes solar-powered robotic lawnmowers and also provides engineering products and solar power development services in New Zealand and the United States.
proceeds: It plans to build a factory in Austin, Texas, and spend on marketing, product development and stock. It will also repay a loan, pay US$2,000,000 for Brightway Energy, and use the rest for working capital.
risks: A lender can convert its loan into shares of a subsidiary, which could dilute the company's ownership and cost it control.
The company has little history of selling its SunScout robotic mower products at large scale, so growth is uncertain.
Growth depends on its own DSA technology being sold successfully and working reliably.
Geopolitical tensions and international trade rules could hurt its business and results.
Political, legal, social and economic conditions in the places it operates or plans to expand could hurt its business.
